title: Maji Maji rebellion
summary: From July 1905 peoples of southern German East Africa rose against German rule, rallied by a spirit medium whose maji water medicine was said to turn bullets. Gale says it was effectively stamped out by August 1907 after a scorched-earth response. Iliffe records an official guess of 75,000 African dead, mostly from famine and disease; Gale estimates 250,000 dead of famine.

uncertainty.note: Iliffe dates the start to the night of 31 July 1905 if counted from the first victims; Gale says open rebellion began in July 1905 and was effectively stamped out in August 1907.

as_recorded.value: it began on the night of 31 July 1905
it was not until August of 1907 that the rebellion was effectively stamped out

where.modern_name: Rufiji region, Pwani, Tanzania (proxy pin: Rufiji district office; the revolt began in the Matumbi Hills and middle and lower Rufiji, then spread across the south and east)
where.historical_name: German East Africa, Rufiji and Matumbi Hills region

importance.justification: Gale calls it the first united, interethnic opposition to colonial rule in Africa and says it led to German administrative reforms.

audience_note: Describes a scorched-earth campaign and famine with very high civilian death tolls.

sources.title: The Organization of the Maji Maji Rebellion

reviewer_note: Death toll shown as two attributed figures, not merged: 75,000 "official guess" (Iliffe 1967, mostly famine and disease) and "an estimated 250,000" from famine (Gale). Pin is a deliberate proxy for a very large area (Iliffe: began in the Matumbi Hills and Madaba, centred on the middle and lower Rufiji); the Matumbi Hills have no coordinate I could source. Only the day 31 July is Iliffe's own dating "from the death of its first victims".
